title: 文化与社会生活词汇
goal: 理解文化与社会生活词汇，并区分社会活动的目的和参与方式。

points.label: 理解文化与社会生活常用词汇
读懂社会活动的目的与实施方式

sources.title: 高考英语（新课标卷）：课表
sources.used: 文化与社会生活词汇、活动目的和参与方式

body.p: 文化与社会生活类材料常介绍文化遗产、社区活动和人与人的交往。读活动介绍时，要分清两件事：活动为什么举办，参与者具体做什么。

body.box: A community centre began a project to preserve local weaving knowledge. Its purpose was to record the methods used by experienced weavers and make those methods available to learners. Volunteers interviewed the weavers and wrote descriptions of their work. The centre then arranged a small workshop where learners could watch a demonstration and ask questions. Participants could also read the written descriptions. The interviews supplied the material; attending the workshop was one way to learn from it. The project did not require every learner to become an interviewer.

body.p: 项目的目的是保存并传播编织方法。志愿者采访和记录，是在收集材料。学习者观看示范、提问、阅读记录，是参与的方式。
preserve 在此表示保存知识。interview 是采访，demonstration 是展示操作方法。

groups.fill: Volunteers planned a local exhibition. They coll{ected} old photo{graphs} and reco{rded} the sto{ries} of peo{ple} who sha{red} them, th{en} prep{ared} a dis{play} for visi{tors}. The owners helped identify places shown in the pictures. Each description named the person who provided the information. The volunteers checked the wording with the owners before opening the exhibition. They also left space for visitors to add comments about places they recognised.
notes: photographs：后文 pictures 指代照片。
stories：照片分享者讲述自己的故事。
shared：与 them 搭配，指分享照片。
then：引出收集和记录之后的行动。
display：后文 exhibition 复现展览。
visitors：后文 visitors 复现参观者。

groups.text:
A community centre started a cooking exchange so that residents could learn how their neighbours prepare familiar dishes. Each month a different volunteer demonstrates a recipe. Participants watch the steps, ask about ingredients and receive a written copy of the method. They may also offer to lead a later session.

The centre asks volunteers to list ingredients before each meeting. This allows participants to check what will be used and helps staff prepare the room. At the end of a session, participants can leave feedback about the explanations or suggest another topic. The centre uses these comments to plan future meetings rather than treating one recipe as the only correct version of a dish.

items.stem: What does a volunteer do when demonstrating a recipe?
options: Shows participants how a dish is prepared
Collects the written copies afterwards
Lists the ingredients after the session
Gives feedback on participants' explanations
items.why: 依据：a different volunteer demonstrates a recipe. Participants watch the steps。demonstrate 指演示做菜的步骤。

items.stem: What is the purpose of the cooking exchange?
options: To choose one correct version of each dish
To learn how neighbours prepare dishes
To replace written recipes with comments
To train volunteers to lead later sessions
items.why: 依据：started a cooking exchange so that residents could learn how their neighbours prepare familiar dishes。so that 引出活动的目的。

items.stem: How can participants take part during a session?
options: By listing the ingredients before the meeting
By preparing the room together with staff
By watching and asking about ingredients
By choosing the one correct recipe version
items.why: 依据：Participants watch the steps, ask about ingredients。参与者观看步骤并询问食材。列食材清单的是志愿者。

items.stem: Why are ingredient lists requested in advance?
options: To let staff choose the correct version of a dish
To let participants offer to lead a later session
To replace the written copy given at the end
So participants can check them and staff can prepare
items.why: 依据：This allows participants to check what will be used and helps staff prepare the room。清单方便参与者核对，也方便工作人员准备场地。

items.stem: How does the centre use participants' comments?
options: It uses them to plan the meetings that follow.
It uses them to choose one correct recipe.
It uses them to decide how to prepare the room.
It uses them to check the ingredient lists.
items.why: 依据：The centre uses these comments to plan future meetings。反馈用于安排之后的活动。

groups.fill: A school organised a music evening. Many par{ents} brought instr{uments} and sha{red} the so{ngs} of th{eir} families wh{ile} students to{ok} notes a{nd} prepared pos{ters} for t{he} exhibition. The posters explained where each song had been learned. Families checked the descriptions before the display opened. During the event, visitors listened to the music and asked questions about the performers' experiences. The school kept the posters so that another group could learn from the project later.

groups.text:
A town community centre began a project to help residents share their experience of moving to the area. The organisers wanted people who had arrived at different times to meet and learn about the services and activities that had helped them settle. They planned a series of small conversation groups rather than a single public lecture.

Before the first meeting, volunteers spoke with residents about topics they would be comfortable discussing. Some suggested finding a place to study; others wanted to talk about meeting neighbours or learning the bus routes. The volunteers used these suggestions to prepare questions, but participants were free to speak about a different experience or simply listen. No one was asked to provide a complete account of their life.

Each group met at the centre with a volunteer who introduced the topic and made sure everyone had an opportunity to speak. Participants could bring a friend, and staff provided information about local classes and clubs on a separate table. The aim was to support conversation, not to require people to join a particular activity.

After the meetings, the organisers invited anonymous written feedback. Several participants said that hearing different experiences helped them identify useful local resources. Others requested meetings at a different time. In response, the centre arranged an additional evening group and continued offering the original daytime meeting. The organisers did not publish individual stories; they used the feedback to improve the format. They also planned to review whether the conversation topics remained useful as new participants joined. The project depended on cooperation between residents, volunteers and centre staff, each contributing in a different way.

items.stem: What does cooperation mean in the final sentence?
options: Different people working together
Residents telling stories of settling in
Groups meeting at different times
Staff giving out information on clubs
items.why: 依据：cooperation between residents, volunteers and centre staff, each contributing in a different way。cooperation 指几方各出一份力、共同合作。

items.stem: What was the project's main purpose?
options: To require residents to join a local club
To let residents share settling experiences
To collect complete accounts of every life
To teach residents the local bus routes
items.why: 依据：a project to help residents share their experience of moving to the area。项目的目的是让居民交流来此安顿的经历。bus routes 只是居民提出的一个话题。

items.stem: How were the initial conversation questions prepared?
options: Staff copied questions from a public lecture.
Residents were required to write life histories.
Volunteers used topics suggested by residents.
Clubs selected one activity for everyone to join.
items.why: 依据：volunteers spoke with residents about topics，又 used these suggestions to prepare questions。问题按居民提出的话题准备。

items.stem: What could a participant do during a group meeting?
options: Publish another person's individual story
Require everyone to join a particular club
Introduce the topic in place of the volunteer
Listen without describing an experience
items.why: 依据：participants were free to speak about a different experience or simply listen。参与者可以只听，不讲自己的经历。

items.stem: How did the centre respond to requests about meeting times?
options: It added an evening group and kept the daytime one.
It replaced every daytime meeting with a lecture.
It published residents' stories before the next meeting.
It stopped collecting feedback about the format.
items.why: 依据：arranged an additional evening group and continued offering the original daytime meeting。中心加开晚间组，日间组照常。
